REQ mixes calendar years, Australian financial years, quarters and months.
`period` is the normalized label; `period_start`, `period_end`,
`period_basis`, and `frequency` make the interpretation explicit.

Status precedence follows the published workbook:

1. suffix (`s`, `f`, `z`);
2. row or column header;
3. title;
4. note or legend;
5. landing-page text;
6. `published-unclassified`.

```{r}
readreq::req_status(c("2025-26s", "2026-27f", "2029-30z", "2024-25"))
```

Units, currencies and price bases are series-key dimensions. Nominal and real
values, CY and FY periods, and AUD and USD values therefore cannot silently
collapse. Literal `na`, unavailable, confidential and suppressed cells produce
numeric `NA` while preserving `raw_value` and `missing_reason`; zero remains a
real published zero.
